threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, baseline approach, and responsibilities for the project.

messages.text:

We need to align on:
- which exact line code and shifts are in scope (D1)
- who owns the mapping of critical machines and failure history (T1)
- who owns the baseline downtime and waste logging (T2)
I suggest we use the existing Project Timeline and Shift Communication Plan in A7 as our reference for dates and check-ins.
Can you confirm if everyone is ok with that scope and with using A7 as our single place for timing and shift communication?

From the operator side, I am fine focusing on the main flow-wrap line only.
For shifts, I recommend we include A, B, and C shifts, since they all run that line and we want consistent logs.
I can take ownership of T2 for the baseline downtime and waste logging, using A1 as the sheet, and I will align with the production supervisor on how to validate it.
Before we lock D1, can someone confirm the exact line code so I can put it on the log header and in A7?

From maintenance, I suggest we define the scope as packaging line PL-01, which is the main chocolate flow-wrap line.
That line runs on shifts A, B, and C, so I agree with including all three.
I can support T1 together with the other mechanics, mapping the machines and pulling the last 3 months of breakdown history from the maintenance logs.

I am ok with focusing on PL-01 and shifts A, B, and C.
For T1, I can start listing all key machines on PL-01 and their basic specs from the line layout and nameplates.
I will need someone to double-check the failure history part, as I am less familiar with the way the logs are structured.
We can then merge my list with the breakdown summary that others pull.

Good, I can help on the failure history for T1.
I will extract the last 3 months of breakdowns for PL-01 from the maintenance system and summarise the top 5 failure modes by frequency and impact.
Then we can combine that with the machine list you prepare so that T1 meets the definition of done.
I will also check that what we do fits with the dates in A7 so we do not clash with planned work.

Thanks for volunteering for T2.
To close D1, I propose we state explicitly:
- Line in scope: PL-01 (main chocolate flow-wrap line)
- Shifts in scope: A, B, and C only
If no one objects in this thread, we will treat that as agreed and record D1.
On responsibilities (D2), I suggest:
- T1 owner: 386277, with support from 11000 and 533175
- T2 owner: 95118, with validation by the production supervisor
Please confirm if you are comfortable with that split so we can also record D2.

I am comfortable owning T2 for PL-01 on shifts A, B, and C.
I will adapt A1 into a simple log that operators can fill in quickly and I will walk through it with at least one operator per shift.
I will also sync with the production supervisor to make sure the baseline period fits the production schedule in A7.
From my side, D1 and D2 as you described work.

I confirm I can own T1 with support from 11000 and 533175.
Plan for T1:
- This week: compile the list of key machines on PL-01 with basic specs
- Early next week: merge with the 3-month breakdown summary and identify the top 5 failure modes
We will keep the timing aligned with A7 so that we finish T1 before we start detailed preventive maintenance planning.
I am ok with D1 and D2 as stated.

I am fine supporting T1 on the breakdown history and failure modes.
Once 386277 and 11000 have the machine list, I will add the failure data and check that we have enough detail to feed into T3 and T6 later.
No concerns from me on D1 and D2.

I am ok supporting T1 as described.
I will start walking the line today to capture the machine list and basic specs, and I will share a draft with 386277 and 533175 for review.
D1 and D2 are clear for me.

Summarising this thread so far:
- D1: Scope confirmed as packaging line PL-01, shifts A, B, and C
- D2: T1 owner is 386277 (support 11000 and 533175); T2 owner is 95118 with production supervisor validation
We will track these in A7 so all shifts see the same picture.
Next step is for T1 and T2 owners to update the channel once their first drafts are ready so we can review together.

I will start the 7-day baseline logging for T2 from the next full production day on PL-01, so that all three shifts are covered.
I will post a short update mid-way with any issues operators raise when using A1.

For T1, I will share the initial machine and failure mode list in this channel before the end of the week.
If we see any gaps that could affect the later preventive maintenance work, we can adjust while we are still in the mapping phase.

threads.thread_goal: Define and finalise preventive maintenance schedule and checklists.

messages.text:
Sharing the first draft of the preventive maintenance schedule for PL-01 for review.
I built it based on the outputs from T1 and the current production calendar in A7, and structured it to feed into T3 and T5.
Key points:
- Daily checks: belts, guards, basic lubrication points, visual leaks
- Weekly checks: sensors cleaning, chain tension, safety interlocks test
- Monthly checks: deeper inspections on bearings, pneumatics, and electrical panels
I also drafted a Preventive Maintenance Checklist in line with A2, and cross-checked with A8 to avoid any conflict with environmental and waste handling rules.
Before we approve anything (D3, D4), I need your feedback on feasibility during planned downtimes and whether the checklist format works for the team.

Thanks for pulling this together.
From a maintenance standpoint, the structure daily/weekly/monthly makes sense for T3 and T5.
A couple of questions before we move toward D3 and D4:
- Are the daily checks realistic within the current shift handover time, especially on C shift?
- For monthly checks, do we have enough planned downtime in A7, or do we need to propose extra windows to the production supervisor?
Also, can you clarify how you used A8 to check environmental and waste handling compliance for T11 items?

Looking at the draft checklist in A2, I think the daily section might be a bit long for the time we usually have before start-up.
For example, checking every single guard screw daily might slow us down.
Maybe we can move some of those to the weekly section so that operators and mechanics can focus on the most critical daily points.
I am not fully sure how that impacts T11, so we might need quality or health and safety to confirm.

On the daily checks, I agree with 11000 that we should keep them tight.
From what I see on PL-01, we can realistically cover lubrication of key points, quick visual checks for leaks, and a fast guard inspection during the pre-start window.
For monthly checks, A7 shows a longer planned stop every four weeks; we can use that for the deeper inspections.
Regarding A8 and T11, I reviewed the waste handling steps in the checklist to ensure we do not create extra risk when draining or disposing of product during maintenance.

From the operator side, the checklist format in A2 is readable, but it would help if we had a very short daily version that can be done at the line, and a more detailed weekly/monthly version for planned stops.
If we align the daily checks with the SOP in A3 later, it will be easier for shifts to remember.
For timing, if we keep daily checks under 10 minutes, it should fit into the current routine without delaying start-up.
I do not see any conflict with hygiene rules, but quality should still review the final version for T11.

Good points.
I can adjust the draft so that:
- Daily checks focus on lubrication of critical points, quick guard and leak checks, and basic sensor cleanliness
- Weekly checks include the more detailed guard fastener checks and full sensor cleaning
This should keep daily work within the 10-minute window that 95118 mentioned.
On A8 and T11, I checked that any waste generated during cleaning or draining is captured in the existing waste handling steps and that we do not bypass any containment or segregation rules.
We will still ask quality and health and safety to sign off before we close D3 and D4.

That adjustment sounds reasonable.
To move toward D3, I propose we treat this updated structure as the final preventive maintenance schedule for T3, provided that:
- Production confirms the windows in A7 are enough for weekly and monthly work
- Quality and health and safety confirm there is no conflict with A8 and GMP
For D4, we need to agree that the checklist format in A2, with the split daily/weekly/monthly, is the one we will roll out.
If no one has further changes, we can record D3 and D4 once we get the external confirmations.

With the daily checks reduced as you described, I am comfortable using this schedule on the line.
The checklist layout in A2 is clear enough for me, especially if we highlight the daily items.
I agree with recording D3 and D4 once production and quality confirm their parts.

I am aligned as well.
The schedule covers the main mechanical and electrical risks we see on PL-01, and the checklist in A2 is practical.
Once we have the sign-offs, we can start a short pilot on one shift to see if any timing issues appear before full rollout.

From the operator side, I am ok with this version.
If we can align the daily checks with the start-up steps in A3 later, it will help with adoption across shifts.
I support recording D3 and D4 once we have confirmation from production and quality.

I have now checked with the production supervisor and quality.
They confirmed that the weekly and monthly windows in A7 are sufficient and that the checklist content is consistent with A8 and GMP.
Based on that, I suggest we formally record:
- D3: Preventive maintenance schedule for PL-01 (daily/weekly/monthly) is approved for implementation under T3
- D4: Maintenance checklist format in A2, with the split daily/weekly/monthly, is approved as the final version for T5
Unless there are objections, we can proceed to pilot the schedule on one shift next week.

Agreed.
D3 and D4 are now confirmed as you summarised.
Next step is to run the pilot on one shift, capture any issues, and then roll out to all shifts if the timing and content work as expected.

threads.thread_goal: Standardise operator SOPs and quality/waste checks across shifts.

messages.text:
I am sharing the draft SOP for PL-01 start-up, changeover, shutdown, and cleaning, plus a draft operator quick guide for quality and waste checks.
The SOP draft is in A3 and is based on inputs from operators on shifts A, B, and C under T4.
The quick guide is in A5 and supports T8 and T9.
Key points in the SOP:
- Clear sequence for pre-start checks, including the daily maintenance items from A2
- Standard steps for changeover to minimise product damage and waste
- Shutdown and cleaning steps aligned with hygiene rules and GMP
For the quick guide, I focused on simple visual checks for raw materials, packaging, and main waste points.
Before we move to approval (D5, D6), I need feedback on clarity and whether anything is missing for your shifts.

I went through the SOP in A3.
The start-up section is clear, but I noticed that the step for checking the flow-wrap film tension is only mentioned under troubleshooting.
On the line, we usually adjust film tension before the first run to avoid product damage.
Maybe we should add that as a standard step in the start-up sequence.
On the quick guide in A5, the pictures for acceptable vs non-acceptable packaging look helpful, but we might need one more example for damaged film rolls.

From a maintenance perspective, I like that the SOP start-up section references the daily checks from A2.
One thing to consider is adding a short note on what to do if an operator finds an issue during those checks, so they know when to call maintenance vs when they can correct it themselves.
For the shutdown and cleaning steps, we should double-check with quality that the sequence matches their expectations, especially around avoiding cross-contamination.
This will be important before we confirm D5 and D6.

I agree with adding the film tension step to the start-up sequence.
Also, in the changeover section of A3, we might want to highlight when to adjust guides and sensors to avoid misalignment that leads to waste.
On the quick guide in A5, could we add a small section on what to record in A1 when we see repeated quality issues, so that it links back to the baseline and later tracking?

Overall, the structure of A3 and A5 looks solid.
To move toward D5 and D6, I suggest we:
- Integrate the agreed daily maintenance checks from A2 into the start-up section as a mandatory step
- Add clear escalation rules for when operators should call maintenance
- Ensure the quick guide in A5 references both A1 for logging and the new SOP for actions
Once we have those tweaks and quality approval, we can confirm D5 (SOP approval) and D6 (final quick guide version).

Thanks for the feedback.
I will update A3 to:
- Add film tension adjustment as a standard start-up step
- Include a short decision tree for when to call maintenance vs correct locally
- Highlight guide and sensor adjustments in the changeover section
For A5, I will add examples of damaged film rolls and a small box explaining what to log in A1 when we see repeated issues.
I will then send both A3 and A5 to quality for review under T4, T8, and T9.

Those changes will help a lot on the floor.
Once quality signs off, I suggest we run through the SOP with one operator from each shift to see if any steps are confusing.
That can also feed into the training sessions for T9.

When you add the decision tree for escalation in A3, please include a note that any repeated mechanical fault should be logged clearly so we can use it later in T6 and T7.
That will help us link operator observations to root cause analysis and setting adjustments.

For the quick guide in A5, maybe we can also add a simple reminder about environmental and waste handling rules, pointing to A8.
That way, when operators remove waste from the line, they remember the correct bins and procedures.

Good point.
I will add a small section in A5 that reminds operators which waste goes where, referencing A8, without overloading the guide.
I have now sent the updated A3 and A5 to quality for review.
Once they confirm that the SOP and guide meet GMP and hygiene requirements, we can finalise D5 and D6.

Quality has now confirmed that A3 and A5 are aligned with GMP and hygiene rules.
Based on that, I propose we record:
- D5: Start-up, changeover, shutdown, and cleaning SOP in A3 is approved for rollout on PL-01 under T4
- D6: Operator quality and waste quick guide in A5 is approved as the final version under T8
Next, we can use these as the basis for the training sessions in T9.

Agreed.
D5 and D6 are clear.
I will now prepare a short briefing using A3 and A5 and schedule sessions with at least two shifts to cover T9.
I will also collect any questions that come up so we can refine the materials if needed.

threads.thread_goal: Discuss recurring faults, root causes, and corrective actions.

messages.text:
I am sharing preliminary findings from the root cause analysis on the top recurring mechanical faults for PL-01 under T6.
The draft report is in A4.
Based on the last 3 months of data from T1 and operator feedback, the top 3 faults are:
1) Film tracking issues causing jams and stoppages
2) Product misalignment leading to sealing defects and waste
3) Intermittent sensor failures causing false stops
For each, A4 lists suspected root causes and contributing factors.
I would like your input on which corrective actions we should prioritise within our timebox (D7), and how we can safely pilot any setting changes under T7.

Looking at A4, all three faults are important, but we probably cannot fully address everything within the current project window.
My first thought is to prioritise actions that both reduce downtime and cut waste.
Film tracking and product misalignment seem to have the biggest combined impact.
For T7, we need to define safe parameter ranges with quality before we touch any settings.
I suggest we focus on:
- Mechanical adjustments and guides for film tracking
- Standardised set-up for product alignment
and treat sensor issues mainly with better checks and replacements for now.

From what I see on the line, film tracking issues cause a lot of short stops and rework.
Often we adjust the film manually, but it does not always hold.
If we can improve the guides or tension settings under T7, that would help.
For product misalignment, sometimes it is linked to how we load the infeed, so maybe part of the fix is in the SOP as well as mechanical changes.

I agree that film tracking and product misalignment should be our main focus.
For sensor failures, many of the issues in A4 look like they can be reduced by better cleaning and positioning, which we already covered in the preventive maintenance checklist.
So for D7, I would propose we prioritise:
1) Film tracking corrective actions
2) Product alignment and infeed set-up
and treat sensor improvements as a secondary action that we continue through the new maintenance routines.

From the operator logs in A1 and our daily experience, I can confirm that film tracking and misalignment are the most painful.
They create both downtime and a lot of waste when packs are not sealed correctly.
If we can stabilise those two, it will make a big difference.
For sensors, the new cleaning checks in A2 already help, so I am ok with treating that as a follow-on improvement rather than a main focus for D7.

Based on your feedback, I suggest the following for D7:
- Priority 1: Implement corrective actions on film tracking (guides, rollers, and tension settings) under T7
- Priority 2: Implement corrective actions on product alignment and infeed set-up, including any SOP tweaks
- Priority 3: Continue sensor improvements mainly through the new maintenance and cleaning routines
For T7, I will work with quality to define safe parameter ranges before we run any pilots.
Does anyone see a reason to change this order?

I support that prioritisation.
It matches the impact we see in A4 and what the team is reporting.
For T7, we should also make sure we log the before and after waste and downtime in A6 so we can show the effect of the changes.

The order works for me.
When we pilot the new film tracking settings, I can be on the line to help monitor how stable they are and note any side effects.
We should also brief operators on what to watch for during the pilot so they can give feedback quickly.

No objections from me.
For product alignment, we might need small mechanical adjustments on the infeed guides and a clearer set-up step in A3.
We can coordinate that with the SOP owner so that the mechanical and procedural changes match.

I am aligned with that order.
When you define the safe parameter ranges for T7, please share them so we can include them in the operator training and SOP.
That will help avoid ad-hoc adjustments that could undo the improvements.

Given the agreement in this thread, I will record:
- D7: Within this project timebox, we prioritise corrective actions on film tracking (Priority 1) and product alignment/infeed set-up (Priority 2) under T7, while handling sensor issues mainly through the new maintenance routines.
Next steps for T7:
- Align safe parameter ranges with quality
- Plan a pilot on one shift, logging results in A6
- If stable, extend to all shifts.

threads.thread_goal: Review post-implementation performance and close the project.

messages.text:
Here is the end-of-project update for PL-01.
We have collected post-implementation data for 7 days using A6 under T10, and compared it to the baseline in A1.
Headline results:
- Unplanned downtime on PL-01 reduced by around 18 percent
- Food waste on the packaging line reduced by around 22 percent
These improvements reflect the new preventive maintenance schedule (T3, T5), the SOP and quick guide (T4, T8, T9), and the setting adjustments from T7.
We now need to decide whether to extend these practices to other lines or shifts (D8), and how to keep monitoring performance via T12.

Looking at A6 vs A1, most of the gain seems to come from fewer film tracking and misalignment issues, which matches what we targeted in T7.
The new preventive maintenance routines from T3 and T5 also reduced small stoppages.
From a maintenance point of view, I think the approach is stable enough to extend to at least one more similar packaging line.
For shifts, all three on PL-01 are already using the new routines, so extension would mainly be to other lines.

From the operator side, feedback on the SOP in A3 and the quick guide in A5 has been positive.
Operators on all three shifts report that the steps are clear and that the daily checks fit into their routine.
Given the results in A6, I would support extending the SOP and quick guide to any other lines that use similar packaging equipment, with minor adaptations.
For D8, I would suggest we start with one additional line and monitor it closely before a wider rollout.

On the floor, we see fewer emergency calls and less rework.
The new checks and settings are now part of our normal routine.
I agree with trying this on another similar line first, so we can see if any adjustments are needed for different layouts.
We should also keep using A6 for a while on PL-01 to make sure the gains hold.

I agree with the cautious approach.
Extending to one more line that has similar equipment and product mix seems like a good next step.
We can reuse most of the maintenance schedule and checklists from T3 and T5, and adapt only where the hardware differs.
For T12, we should update A7 to include the new line and keep the same rhythm of updates.

Based on the data in A6 and your feedback, I propose the following for D8:
- Extend the new preventive maintenance schedule, SOP, quick guide, and settings approach to one additional packaging line with similar equipment
- Keep PL-01 under monitoring with A6 for at least another 4 weeks
- Use T12 to coordinate the timeline and communication across shifts for the new line
If we see similar improvements on the second line, we can then consider a broader rollout.

I support that proposal.
From a maintenance resource point of view, extending to one more line is manageable, especially if we reuse most of the materials.
We just need to coordinate the maintenance windows in A7 with production for the new line.

I am aligned.
For the new line, I can adapt the operator parts of A3 and A5 and plan short briefings under T9.
We will also keep logging downtime and waste in A6 so we can compare with the baseline once we have it.

No objections from me.
I can help with the initial checks and adjustments on the new line, similar to what we did on PL-01.
Keeping PL-01 under monitoring for a few more weeks is a good idea to make sure the results are stable.

I agree with D8 as you described.
We should also capture a short summary of lessons learned in A7 so that when we extend further, we remember what worked well and what needed adjustment.

Given the agreement in this thread, I will record:
- D8: We will extend the new maintenance schedule, SOP, quick guide, and settings approach from PL-01 to one additional similar packaging line, while continuing to monitor PL-01 with A6 for at least 4 more weeks, and coordinating via T12.
This closes the main project scope for PL-01.
We will use the next few weeks to stabilise and prepare for the extension.
